description: 🚀 We are Astro Builders, a team of enthusiastic Civil Engineering students passionate about space exploration, science and innovation. We enjoy research, creative thinking and problem-solving. We welcome members with skills in coding, graphic design, research, data analysis, content writing and presentation. Beginners are welcome! Let's learn, collaborate and build something extraordinary together! 🌍
summary: The Silent Legacy is an interactive digital storytelling project by Team CORE that explores NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Instead of treating these objects simply as discarded hardware, our project explains the purpose, engineering role, and lasting significance of each component. We focus on Apollo 11 lunar hardware, including the Lunar Module descent stage and lunar laser-ranging retroreflector, and the Mars 2020 Perseverance landing system, including its heat shield, parachute, backshell, and powered descent stage. Through a visual virtual-museum experience, visitors can explore object stories, mission timelines, comparisons, images, and NASA resources. The project aims to make planetary exploration easier to understand while showing how spacecraft components can become scientific, engineering, and historical evidence after their primary mission is complete.
details: The Silent Legacy: Humanity’s Footprints on the Moon and Mars The Silent Legacy is an interactive digital storytelling project that explores human-made spacecraft hardware left on the Moon and Mars after successful space missions. The project presents this equipment as a virtual museum, helping visitors understand why these objects remain on other worlds and what they tell us about exploration. The project focuses on two major mission stories: Apollo 11 on the Moon and NASA’s Perseverance mission on Mars. The Moon section explains the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage and the lunar laser-ranging retroreflector. The Mars section explores landing-system components associated with Perseverance, including the heat shield, parachute, backshell, and powered descent stage. Rather than presenting these objects simply as “space junk,” the project explains their different purposes. Some were mission hardware designed for one-time use, while others were intentionally deployed for scientific research. The website connects these objects with the engineering decisions, scientific goals, and historical importance of planetary exploration. The project is designed for students, teachers, families, and anyone interested in space science. It uses simple explanations, visual storytelling, object cards, timelines, comparisons, and an easy-to-navigate virtual museum structure to make the subject accessible to beginners. The project also highlights an important idea for future exploration: as humans continue sending missions to the Moon and Mars, the hardware left behind can become part of the scientific and historical record of exploration. Understanding what is intentionally left behind helps us think about responsible exploration and the long-term legacy of human activity beyond Earth. Technologies and tools: HTML, CSS, digital presentation tools, online research resources, and NASA mission information. Creativity and innovation: The project transforms technical mission information into a virtual museum experience. Instead of only listing spacecraft components, it tells the story of each object, its purpose, and its connection to human exploration. Expected impact: The project aims to improve awareness of planetary exploration, encourage interest in STEM subjects, and help students understand the engineering and scientific significance of spacecraft hardware beyond Earth. Tagline: “The machines may stop. The discoveries continue.”
